title: The diagonal of a smooth morphism is Koszul regular and perfect
statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let f:X\to S be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] whose diagonal is a closed immersion (that is, f is separated) and whose pure relative dimension is d. Then the diagonal \Delta:X\to X\times_S X [def-pc-base-change] is a Koszul-regular immersion of codimension d, meaning that locally its defining ideal is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. In particular \Delta is a perfect immersion, meaning that \Delta_*\mathcal O_X is locally a perfect complex over X\times_S X [def-pc-perfect-complex]; since X and S are Noetherian, \Delta is also proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tags 067U (smooth diagonal is Koszul regular) and 068C (perfect and proper immersion consequences)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-smooth-diagonal-regular-immersion] to obtain an affine neighbourhood U of each point. The ideal is the kernel I of the diagonal map on sections; either I is the unit ideal or a regular list of length d generates I. On each U the map on sections of the closed immersion is surjective. Its kernel lift is bijective by the first isomorphism theorem, and the induced spectrum isomorphism composed with the affine spectrum isomorphism gives Delta^{-1}(U) = Spec(Gamma(U)/I). Naturality of Opens.toSpecGamma proves the equality of the two maps to Spec(Gamma(U)).

In the regular-list case, index the list by Fin(length) using List.get. List.ofFn_get preserves its order and regularity, and the range is exactly its membership set, so the span is I. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular], IsRegular.isKoszulRegular. In the unit-ideal case use the singleton 1, whose span is the unit ideal and which is weakly regular since multiplication by 1 is injective. Apply the weak-regular module assertion isKoszulRegularOn_of_isWeaklyRegular of the same node with M = R. The tensor-unit maps TensorProduct.rid give a degreewise isomorphism of complexes, commuting with the differentials by R-linearity. Transport homology vanishing along this isomorphism. Retain the alternative I = top or length = d in both cases.

Discard only the codimension alternative from each affine witness and apply [lem-sc-koszul-regular-closed-immersion-perfect] to the diagonal. Its final conjunct gives perfectness of the degree-zero pushed-forward structure sheaf. The cited Lean theorem does not require a Noetherian target, so no Noetherianity argument for the fibre product is needed.

The diagonal is a closed immersion by hypothesis, so the Mathlib instance for properness of a closed immersion gives IsProper (pullback.diagonal f) directly. Combine it with the local quotient presentations and the perfectness conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_diagonal_koszul_regular_perfect_proper {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsNoetherian S] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsClosedImmersion (pullback.diagonal f)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (pullback f f).toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : (pullback f f).Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings (pullback f f).toRingedSpace).over U))] : (∀ y : (pullback f f : Scheme.{u}), ∃ U : (pullback f f).Opens, y ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∃ (I : Ideal (Γ(pullback f f, U))) (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → Γ(pullback f f, U)), I = Ideal.span (Set.range g) ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular g ∧ (∃ e : Scheme.Opens.toScheme ((pullback.diagonal f) ⁻¹ᵁ U) ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of (Γ(pullback f f, U) ⧸ I)), (pullback.diagonal f) ∣_ U ≫ U.toSpecΓ = e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) ∧ (I = ⊤ ∨ r = d)) ∧ Scheme.IsPerfect (pullback f f) ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (pullback f f).toRingedSpace)) 0).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.diagonal f)).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))) ∧ IsProper (pullback.diagonal f)
